subject: Design review: sealed-key routing and on-prem BYOK handoff

Subject: Design review: sealed-key routing and on-prem BYOK handoff

Hi Sam/Bob,

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Per our call, attached is a concise design proposal for the BYOK handoff and sealed-key routing for your on-prem deployment. High-level points: 

- BYOK model: customer provides a root key material (BYOK) that is imported into the on-prem HSM and used as the top-level wrapping key. Redwood will never see the unwrapped BYOK in our hosted control plane.
- Sealed-key approach: service keys (model-serving AES keys / envelope keys) are generated in the HSM, then wrapped under the BYOK and stored in the customer Vault; unsealing requires HSM-on-prem and a short-lived unseal token.
- Rotation: re-wrap/rotate service keys inside HSM. We propose a rolling rotation that does not export plaintext keys (re-wrap-only pattern). See attachments for sequence diagram.
- Operator access & unseal: operator actions are via a hardened bastion and require MFA + Just-in-Time approval. HSM unseal requires quorum from two operator roles and the provisioned on-site attestation certificate.
- Network: HSM and Vault in isolated compute zone, no outbound internet from HSM network. Control-plane RPCs go over an mTLS tunnel to your control plane endpoint; all traffic limited to specific ports.

Attachments: redwood_sealed_key_flow_v1.pdf, network-zone-diagram.png (diagram shows segmentation and egress controls)

Open questions for your team: rotation window tolerance, preferred HSM vendor (Thales/Luna/Entrust), and audit log retention (for SOC2 evidence).

Proposed next step: we can run an on-site handoff workshop and capture the SOW if this pattern aligns. I'll loop in Markus and Dylan for the technical runbook.

Thanks,

--

Monica,

Thanks for the doc. A few immediate clarifying questions before we sign off on the pattern: 

1) HSM model and certification: do you have an explicit list of validated HSM models and FIPS levels? We need FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or equivalent.
2) Rotation SLA: when you say "rolling rotation," how long would a rotation take and what are the expected service impacts (if any)?
3) Unsealed key lifetime: what is the maximum in-memory lifetime for unwrapped keys? Are they stored in RAM only inside the HSM process space?
4) Audit evidence: we will need tamper/evidence logs and a way to export signed audit trails for internal compliance review.

Also, please send a checklist of what our ops team must prepare for the on-site handoff so we can estimate calendar effort.

Best,

Folks,

Looping in our proposed tech clarifications to answer Sam's questions. See inline: 

- HSM models/cert: we validate Luna HSM (nShield/Luna) and Thales nShield for customer on-prem installs. Both meet FIPS 140-2 L3 in our standard reference. We'll provide the exact firmware/serial model list in the SOW.

- Rotation SLA: rotation is a re-wrap inside the HSM: typical rolling window for a single key family is ~5-10 minutes (no plaintext leaves HSM). Full fleet rotation (all serving keys across zones) depends on concurrency and can be scheduled off-peak; estimate 2–3 hours with zero planned downtime because we re-wrap keys ahead of serving instance switching.

- Unsealed key lifetime: unwrapped keys are held only in HSM volatile memory. For operations that need plaintext (e.g., initial key provisioning), the HSM process exposes a short-lived unseal token. We enforce a maximum in-memory TTL of 30 seconds for any exported ephemeral key material and preferentially use HSM-native crypto ops (no export).

- Audit logs: HSM produces signed event logs (tamper-evident). We will forward signed audit bundles to your secure S3/R2 bucket over the mTLS tunnel on a scheduled cadence. We also emit attestation certificates during unseal events.

- Operator access: propose using a hybrid model: approved JIT sessions via Vault (time-limited SSH certs), operator quorum for unseal, and automated re-seal triggers if inactivity or metrics thresholds hit.

I attached a short SOP for rotation and emergency key-recovery flow (rotation-sop.md).

If agreeable, Dylan and Hiro can prepare the SOW appendix with the serial numbers, networking ACLs, and the exact command sequences we'll run during the handoff.

-Markus
